Author: Claude
Message:
Add Figma extraction pipeline and derived design context

The design file behind the Batch 1 journeys (For Client Review,
JyLGAaO88ELjnyVF2FQ3Bx) had only a depth-limited skeleton committed as
docs/figma_file_structure.json: 203 nodes, 168 top-level frames, but two
text strings and 184 containers with an empty child list. Page 868:21686
("Batch 1 VD") resolves to three empty sections, so no screen content,
colour, typography or component structure was actually available.

Adds scripts/figma/figma-extract.py, which pulls a file once from the
Figma REST API and derives the raw JSON, a text-content dump, design
tokens, a frame inventory and a context brief from that single fetch.
Stdlib only, token read from FIGMA_TOKEN and never written to disk,
retries on 429/5xx. A --from-json mode re-derives every output from a
saved API response without calling the API.

Runs that mode over the existing skeleton to publish what can be derived
today under docs/design/figma/. The generated CONTEXT.md states plainly
that the extract is incomplete and counts the truncated containers, so a
reader cannot mistake "empty frame" for "not fetched".

The extraction could not be completed in-session: api.figma.com is not on
the egress allowlist, and the policy proxy refuses CONNECT with a 403 for
the whole figma.com domain. docs/design/figma/README.md records the
blocker and the exact command to finish the pull from a networked host.

Regenerates DOC-MAP.yaml so the five new documents are routed.

Author: Claude
Message:
Add combined Dockerfile for 1sb-integration-service + bank-persistence-service

Single-image build for standalone cloud validation: packages both service
jars, starts bank-persistence-service (:8081, in-memory H2 by default) first
and waits for its liveness probe, then starts 1sb-integration-service (:8080)
against it over localhost. Lets a cloud deployment be hit directly via the
1SB Swagger UI (http://<host>:8080/swagger-ui.html) to validate the
integration end-to-end without standing up two separate containers.
